last_analysis: No scores are visible. Every trial trained cleanly, so nothing here can be ranked on evidence; only reasoning separates them. Three things should help. First, the per-layer footprint features fit the drop rule. Second, fewer PPO epochs buy more fresh designs (2 epochs gives about 1.8x the samples) and more updates, which should help on held-out designs. Third, build-wide context should help with placement order. r3c3 combines all three. Its 1.17x compute keeps it fast, so it is the base for this round. As this is the last round, I chose three candidates that differ in kind so the final selection has distinct options: (a) push the sample-count idea to 1 epoch; (b) use a longer reward horizon for the exact-build bonus, plus less entropy so greedy play is sharper; (c) feed the legality mask and the layer above each cell into the network, so it can see overhang and height-limit structure.
